Title: Congress-Bundestag Youth Exchange (CBYX)
Organization: U.S. Department of State / German Bundestag
Description: Fully funded scholarship from the U.S. Congress and German Bundestag for American high school students to spend an academic year in Germany, living with a host family and attending a German school.

Title: FLEX Global Abroad
Organization: U.S. Department of State / American Councils
Description: Fully funded State Department program for U.S. citizens in grades 9-12 (aged 15 to 18.5 at the start) to spend the 2027-28 academic year abroad, living with a host family and attending a local high school. It places students in ten countries, among them Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Morocco, Poland, Romania and Thailand. Airfare, host-family room and board, insurance, visa fees and a monthly stipend are covered. It replaces YES Abroad.
Link and status check: Live 2026-10-08. Replaces YES Abroad (yes-abroad.org sends 2027-28 applicants here); application deadline Nov 30, 2026

Title: MIT THINK Scholars Program
Description: Submit a STEM research or invention proposal. Finalists get weekly mentorship, up to $1,000 in project funding and, where possible, an all-expenses-paid trip to MIT. Open to high school students with a permanent U.S. address.
Link and status check: Live 2026-10-07. Page still shows the 2025-26 cycle (opened Nov 1, due Jan 1); 2026-27 dates not yet posted

Title: Stanford Medical Youth Science Program (SMYSP)
Description: Tuition-free, five-week immersive medicine and health program at Stanford for low-income and first-generation high school juniors from Northern California.

Title: College Prep Scholars Program
Description: For high-achieving juniors from households earning under $65,000 a year (family of four). Scholars get summer program scholarships, admissions conferences, free college visits and a head start on QuestBridge's National College Match in senior year.

Title: National Student Poets Program
Description: A national honor for young poets. Each year, five teens are chosen as youth poetry ambassadors for their region. Students in grades 10–11 who win a Gold Key for poetry in the Scholastic Awards may be invited to apply.

Title: Princeton Prize in Race Relations
Description: Recognizes high school students who have shown leadership in advancing racial equity or promoting racial understanding in their schools or communities.

Title: Air Force Academy Summer Seminar
Description: A week living like a cadet at the U.S. Air Force Academy, for high school juniors thinking about a service academy. About 320 students are selected per session, and the program fee is $400.

Title: Texas Aerospace Scholars
Description: NASA program for Texas juniors and seniors who are U.S. citizens. It runs as an online course with NASA engineers, then a virtual summer challenge, and the top teams go to a residential experience at Johnson Space Center. There is no cost to selected students.

Title: Math Prize for Girls
Description: Invitation-only contest at MIT with $100,000 in prizes, including $50,000 for first place. Open to girls in 11th grade or below living in North America who took the AMC 10 or 12 the previous November. The top 300 applicants are invited.

Title: Eisenman Materials Camp
Description: Free, week-long materials science camp at ASM International's headquarters for students entering 11th or 12th grade. Includes team problem-solving, lab work and field trips, with meals and hotel lodging covered.

Title: American Regions Mathematics League (ARML)
Description: National high school math team competition held at the same time at five U.S. university sites each spring: Penn State, the University of Iowa, the University of Nevada, Reno, Western Carolina University and Saint Anselm College. The 2026 contest was on May 31. Students compete on 15-person regional or school teams.
Link and status check: Live 2026-10-08. 2026 contest held May 31; blurb corrected from June

Title: National History Bee and Bowl
Description: History quiz competitions for individuals (Bee) and school teams (Bowl). Students qualify through an online exam and regional tournaments for the National Championships in Arlington, Virginia, on April 24–25, 2027.

Title: Cal Grant
Description: California's main state grant for college, which does not have to be repaid. Seniors qualify by filing the FAFSA or California Dream Act Application (CADAA) by the March 2 priority deadline. Both applications for 2027-28 open October 1, 2026.

Title: Florida Bright Futures Scholarship
Description: Florida's merit scholarship for in-state college. Students earn it by completing the required coursework, test scores and service hours, and must submit the Florida Financial Aid Application (FFAA) in senior year.

Title: Edison Scholars Program
Description: $50,000 college scholarships for 30 high school seniors each year who plan to study STEM at a four-year college. Applicants need at least a 3.0 GPA, financial need, and a home in Southern California Edison's service area. The 2027 application opens this fall.
